case_name: M/S. Pankaj Jain Agencies v Union Of India And Other
respondent:
Union Of India And Other
Supreme Court of India

14 July 1994
W.P. No. 123 of 1987
The Judgment was delivered by : M. N. Venkatachaliah, J.
1. These notifications relate to rates of customs duty on the imports of parts, components and sub-assemblies of Ball Bearings and Roller Bearings. The impugned notification specifically relates to 'parts' of Ball and Roller Bearings.

facts: The petitioner, M/s Pankaj Jain Agencies, assails the vires of the Notification No. 142/86-Cus. dated 13-2-1986 of the Central Government issued in exercise of powers u/s. 25(1) of the Customs Act, 1962.
The notification relates to rates of customs duty on the imports of parts, components and sub-assemblies of Ball Bearings and Roller Bearings.

The petitioner carries on business of imports of component parts of Ball and Roller Bearings and claims to be the beneficiary by assignment and transfer of certain replenishment licences initially issued in favour of M/s Geo Millers & Co. Pvt. Ltd., New Delhi.

Pursuant thereto, the petitioner claims to have entered into an agreement with M/s Business Birds, Singapore, for the supply of 'cups' of Chinese manufacture and said to be component parts of Ball Bearings.
The foreign supplier shipped the goods in three different lots from Singapore to Bombay Port.
issues: Is the impugned notification ultra vires the powers of the Central Government u/s. 25(1) of the Customs Act, 1962?
Did the impugned notification impose a fresh and nascent duty on spare parts or components of Ball Bearings which were not originally brought to charge in the statute?
Is the enhancement brought about by the impugned notification an unreasonable restriction on petitioner's fundamental rights u/art. 19(1)(g)?
petitioner_arguments: The import was complete even before the impugned notification can be said to have come into force as the impugned notification was not made known to those who were likely to be affected by it.
The impugned notification insofar as it prescribed import duty on parts of Ball Bearings, is ultra vires the powers of the Central Government u/s. 25(1) of the Customs Act, 1962.
The enhancement brought about by the impugned notification, so far as the present consignments were concerned, was to raise the petitioner's liability from Rs 1,84,341 to Rs 6,42,065.
court_reasoning: The relevant statutory provisions relating to the rates of duty on imports of Ball Bearings and Roller Bearings and parts thereof under the Customs Tariff Act, 1975.
The impugned notification did not prescribe a rate higher than the statutory duty.

The contention of Shri Ganesh that the relevant date with reference to which the rates of customs duty require to be ascertained had already occurred by the time the impugned notification No. 142/86-Cus. came into force is, on the facts of the present case, clearly untenable.
holding: The impugned notification did not impose a fresh and nascent duty on spare parts or components of Ball Bearings which were not originally brought to charge in the statute.
The enhancement brought about by the impugned notification was not an unreasonable restriction on petitioner's fundamental rights u/art. 19(1)(g).
The impugned notification did not prescribe a rate higher than the statutory duty.
